- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or shows negative momentum — model fails to capture downward drift.
- Lagged corrections: if true price drops after a forecast spike, reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strong.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles — cap forecast at 10% below 30-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- Spike recovery: after a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days unless sentiment remains bullish.
